chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ibn Abi Najran from Al-Muthanna from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The 'Mambudh' (foundling) is free; if he wishes, he may attach himself to the one who picked him up, and it is binding; and if he wishes, he may attach himself to another, and it is binding; and if the one who raised him seeks him, he provides for his maintenance. If he is wealthy, he returns him; and if he is not wealthy, whatever he spent becomes charity.

key_terms.الْالْتِقَاءُ: The act of picking up / finding
key_terms.يُوَالِيَ: To attach oneself to / to choose as a guardian

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for a foundling (Mambudh) regarding freedom, guardianship, and financial maintenance in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the emancipation status of the *Mambudh* (foundling), emphasizing their freedom to choose between their finder or another guardian. It establishes a nuanced financial liability where the guardian's wealth determines whether maintenance costs are a debt to be repaid or a permanent charitable act (*Sadaqah*), reflecting the Shia juristic focus on equitable social welfare. The ruling underscores the child's autonomy in guardianship while balancing the economic realities of the caretaker.
